extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and practitioners in finance, corporate governance, and securities regulation (event-study researchers, regulators, and corporate lawyers)
extracted.subtask_description: Measuring market valuation effects (abnormal returns, cumulative abnormal returns, dollar losses) and decomposing total share-value losses into fine effects, class-action effects, readjustment effects, and reputation loss for firms subject to federal enforcement actions for financial misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of enforcement action types and legal provisions cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize each enforcement action by the financial reporting provision cited (e.g., books & records charges (no internal controls), internal controls charges (no books & records), both internal controls and books & records charges, circumvention charges) and by enforcement/action characteristics (no fraud vs fraud included; civil fraud vs criminal fraud; charges under the 1933 Securities Act, 1934 Securities Exchange Act, or both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use original enforcement filings/proceedings to classify actions; report counts and cross-tabulate by category to examine heterogeneity in market responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of abnormal return (AR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abnormal return is computed by subtracting the CRSP value-weighted index return of all stocks from the raw return of the firm’s equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the value-weighted CRSP index as the market benchmark. Calculate parametric t-statistics for mean abnormal returns using the cross-sectional standard error of abnormal returns. Also report median abnormal returns and significance using the Mann-Whitney rank-sum test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event identification: trigger events and regulatory/investigation events
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify trigger events (events in federal proceedings that reveal the violation) and distinguish investigation events (announced by the firm as informal inquiries or formal investigations), regulatory events (official administrative or litigation releases by the SEC or DOJ), and resolution disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trigger events include self-disclosures of accounting irregularity, restatements, auditor departures, unusual trading, and other federal investigation-related announcements. Count unique announcement dates (#Ann) and # with returns data (#w/Data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of missing returns and delisted firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sample firms are never listed on CRSP and others are delisted during their enforcement period; number of returns differs across event dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how many trigger/regulatory/investigation events have CRSP returns available. Recognize that measuring returns only for surviving firms and on specific dates almost certainly understates total valuation losses; present this as a conservative bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of one-day market-adjusted returns for announcement effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Report average one-day market-adjusted returns for enforcement-related announcements (grouped by announcement type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present mean, median, percent negative, and p-values for t-tests and Mann-Whitney tests. Use one-day returns to identify immediate market reaction to specific announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical inference for abnormal returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate parametric t-statistics based on cross-sectional standard errors and use Mann-Whitney rank-sum tests for medians/signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report p-values (e.g., P > |t| and P > |s|) and significance thresholds (the paper emphasizes significance at the 0.001 level for many comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative Abnormal Return (CAR) for an enforcement action
rubrics_metrics.description: For each enforcement action j, CAR_j is defined as the sum over e = 1..n_j of AR_{j,e}, where AR_{j,e} is the abnormal return on enforcement event date e (e=1 initial event date; e=n_j final event date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumulate abnormal returns only over specific announcement dates (not the entire enforcement period) to improve signal-to-noise ratio and avoid artifacts from long enforcement windows and delistings. Provide mean and median CARs and convert CARs into dollar losses by multiplying each AR by the firm’s market capitalization one day before the announcement and summing across event dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of abnormal returns to dollar losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform abnormal returns into dollar losses by multiplying each AR_{j,e} by the firm’s market capitalization one day before the announcement date e, and summing over event dates for each firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mean dollar loss per firm and aggregate dollar losses across the sample. Acknowledge that delistings and missing returns can understate aggregate losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitioning total share-value loss into components
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose total change in firm value ΔV_t into Fine Effect, Class-Action Effect, Readjustment Effect, and Reputation Loss: ΔV_t = Fine Effect + Class-Action Effect + Readjustment Effect + Reputation Loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate each observable component (fines, class-action settlements, readjustment) and treat the residual as reputation loss under rational expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readjustment effect definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Readjustment Effect = Observed V_{t-1} − Correct V_{t-1} = V(I_Incorrect_{t-1}) − V(I_Correct_{t-1}), i.e., the portion of observed share-value decline that reflects correction of previously misleading accounting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate with asset or earnings restatement examples; compute using asset-based and earnings-based approaches and report sensitivity to assumptions about multiples (market-to-book or P/E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset-based readjustment measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate readjustment by taking the largest annual book value write-off during the enforcement period (sum of Compustat items #17 special items, #183 accounting changes, and #349 net charge-offs for banks) and converting to market value by multiplying by the industry median market-to-book ratio (two-digit SIC) for the corresponding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtract monetary penalties from net charge-offs when present to avoid double counting. For missing Compustat items set values equal to zero. Use weighted-average industry medians and report mean/median/aggregate readjustment estimates. Discuss that some write-offs may be unrelated to the deception (e.g., restructuring), which tends to overstate readjustment (conservative for reputation estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings-based readjustment (alternative) and robustness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Also compute alternative readjustment estimates using earnings restatements multiplied by P/E multiples, and run sensitivity analyses to varying assumptions about whether market-to-book or P/E multiples change when misconduct becomes public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report that results are qualitatively similar across approaches; emphasize asset-based approach because it excludes fewer firms and produces larger readjustment (hence more conservative reputation-loss estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of class-action and derivative lawsuit payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Count class-action/derivative lawsuits and payments; net amounts paid to firms as a result of derivative actions out of monetary penalty tallies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number of lawsuits and payment totals; present means/medians and note large outliers (e.g., Cendant, WorldCom) and sensitivity when excluding outliers from means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloging non-monetary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Record non-monetary sanctions imposed (SEC administrative sanctions like cease-and-desist orders, injunctive sanctions, trading suspensions, registration revocations) and report counts and share of total non-monetary actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that many non-monetary sanctions (e.g., cease-and-desist orders) appear to impose very small penalties and are common; report totals (e.g., 801 non-monetary sanctions across 585 firms) and how many firms had criminal indictments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational expectations assumption for decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume that actual fines, class-action settlements, and observed readjustments are unbiased estimates of investors’ expectations of these amounts at the time news becomes public; thus the residual after subtracting them from ΔV_t is attributed to reputation loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state this identification assumption and use it to justify treating the residual as the present value of impaired operations, higher cost of capital, diverted managerial resources, and other reputational effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel/sample construction and survival adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results for multiple panels: (A) firms with returns and Compustat data available for at least one enforcement date, (B) subset listed on both CRSP and Compustat, (C) firms that survived enforcement period as independent entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mean, median, and aggregate statistics separately for these panels to show influence of delisting/failure. Note that survivors tend to be larger and that delisted firms’ losses are understated because returns are missing after delisting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative measurement choices and bias acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt measurement choices that tend to produce conservative (smaller) estimates of reputation loss — e.g., cumulating only over identifiable announcement dates, using asset-based readjustment which yields larger readjustment (thus smaller residual reputation loss), and setting missing Compustat items to zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document these choices and emphasize that the resulting reputation loss estimates are likely lower bounds due to sample selection and measurement conservatism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of descriptive statistics and sensitivity to outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Report means, medians, aggregate sums, min/max, and comment on extreme observations that materially affect means (e.g., WorldCom fine, Cendant settlement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide statistics both including and excluding outliers and discuss effects on interpretation (e.g., mean fines drop substantially when outliers excluded).
